summary.text: Norcold absorption refrigerators cool on 120 volt AC or propane, and 3-way models add 12 volt DC. Their electronic controls choose an energy source in AUTO mode and report faults on the control panel; on models such as the 1200 series these are two-part codes like "no" "FL" in the center display with an audible alarm.

models.text: N41X (4.5 cu. ft.) and N51X (5.5 cu. ft.) come as 2-way or 3-way; 3-way model numbers include ".3" and 2-way numbers do not.
N400X (4.5 cu. ft.) and N510X (5.5 cu. ft.) are 2-way or 3-way refrigerators; 3-way model numbers include ".3".
N61X (6 cu. ft.) and N81X (8 cu. ft.) are 2-way refrigerators.
N62X/N82X are 2-way; N64X/N84X are 2-way or 3-way; N64XIM/N84XIM are 2-way with ice maker (6 and 8 cu. ft.).
N109X is a 10 cu. ft. 2-way refrigerator and N109XIM adds an ice maker; the letter "X" in a model number stands for a letter or numeral meaning a refrigerator option.
1200XX models are 12.0 cu. ft., 2-way, 4-door refrigerators; 120X-IMXX models add an ice maker.
On gas absorption models the model tag is inside the refrigerator on the right-hand side of the cabinet above the top shelf.
1200 series HTS recall 10E-049 covers 1200LR, 1200LRIM, 1201LRIM, 1210 and 1211 produced January 1, 2003 to October 6, 2010 within listed refrigerator and cooling-unit serial ranges.

display.text: N41X/N51X show single-letter fault codes in the center display ("F", "A", "C", "n", "H", "r", "S"); "No display" means DC voltage is unavailable or the refrigerator is OFF.
N61X/N81X have no letter display: faults show as the ON light and GAS light flashing about once per second, or the ON light flashing off 1, 3 or 4 times about every 3 seconds.
N109X shows two-part codes in the center display, such as "no" "FL" or "dc" "LO", most with an audible alarm; "dr" means the door was open more than 2 minutes.
If an available energy source is not operating correctly, a fault code shows and the controls try a less efficient source; if none is available, an alarm starts and a fault code shows.
Cooling unit sensing: if the controls sense the cooling unit has stopped cooling, the heat sources are turned off and locked out, an alarm starts and "no" "co" shows.
Backup operating system: if the temperature sensor fails it keeps cooling; on N41X/N51X the temperature setting flashes for ten seconds when TEMP SET is pushed.
High Temperature Sensor light: slow flashing (1 flash per second) means low DC power; fast flashing (2-3 flashes per second) means a break in the thermistor wire.
Door alarm that keeps sounding: the door was open longer than 2 minutes; other causes are a sagging door, a bad door switch or a warped door.

reset.text: A "no" "co" lockout can be reset one time: hold ON/OFF two seconds to turn off, then push and release ON/OFF to restart.
The 1200 table splits "no" "co": 1st time, before reset, owner checks; 2nd time, after reset, not owner serviceable.
N61X/N81X: reset by turning the refrigerator OFF and then back to AUTO or GAS mode.
2118 "Sr": turn the refrigerator power OFF and back on to reset; if the code continues, see a dealer or authorized Norcold Service Center.
Some Norcold units need the on/off button held 3-5 seconds to turn on or off.

checks.text: Burner did not ignite: check the propane tank valve is open, gas is at the correct pressure, the refrigerator's manual shutoff valve is open, and there is no air in the supply line.
AC not available: check the refrigerator is plugged into a serviceable outlet, the vehicle fuse or circuit breaker is intact, and the generator is operational (if applicable).
Low DC voltage: check the vehicle battery charging equipment and the AC/DC converter (if applicable) are operational.
3-way DC operation: run on DC only with the engine running; with the engine running, DC supply leads at the refrigerator should read more than 11.5 VDC.
12V only works with the engine running on the N3100 and N4100, whose DC supply is linked to the engine battery.
Poor AC cooling: the setting may be too low for the outside temperature; Norcold refrigerators need at least 115V on both sides of the fuse to perform as expected on AC.
At a destination, make sure the unit is level (no more than 3 degrees side to side or 6 degrees front to back) and that AC is 30 amp service or greater.
Backup operating system: check freezer and fresh food temperatures are satisfactory; allow about one hour after each setting change before checking.
Defrost by turning the refrigerator off, opening the doors and laying towels; never use a heat gun, hair dryer or boiling water, which damage the interior.
For odors, place a bowl of water with pure vanilla extract inside; charcoal, wet newspapers or baking soda also help. Never use harsh household cleaners.

parts.text: N61X/N81X have a temperature switch for overheating protection; a Norcold authorized service technician can determine if it has been triggered.
On 2118 models "oP" "LI" means a temperature limit switch is open; this is not owner serviceable.
The High Temperature Sensor (HTS kit) is a national NHTSA safety recall; parts are shipped to and installed by a trained service technician, not sent to consumers.
Outside the HTS recall serial ranges, Norcold's Temperature Monitor Control (TMC), part 637360, is available at the consumer's cost.
parts.locator: '1200 Series High Temperature Sensor Recall' note

parts.text: N61X/N81X: if the AC heater fails, the refrigerator operates on propane only and the fault is not owner serviceable.

callTech.text: If you smell gas: open windows, do not light the appliance, put out open flames, do not touch switches or use phones, evacuate, shut off fuel at the LP tank, call emergency services.
If "no" "co" returns before a full cooling cycle completes, it cannot be reset; have the refrigerator serviced by a dealer or Norcold authorized Service Center as soon as possible.
If the burner does not ignite on propane after two or three attempts, stop and consult your local dealer or an authorized Norcold Service Center.
Solid red High Temperature Sensor light: the HTS kit has tripped; turn off the refrigerator, unplug it from the 110V outlet and contact a Norcold service center.
Never bypass, alter or modify electrical components, including the HTS system; it can remove safety protection. Have the refrigerator diagnosed by a service center.

1200 series recall units with an un-performed recall or a tripped HTS: set controls OFF, unplug through the outside service vent, disconnect shore power, and do not operate until professionally repaired.

Norcold LLC filed Chapter 11 in late 2025. Warranty claims for units sold before November 3, 2025 go to Dave Carter & Associates; recall matters go to the Liquidating Trustee's counsel, Brinkman Law Group.
Freezer frost or condensation: Thetford does not give consumers technical advice on this; have it diagnosed at a Norcold Authorized Service Center.
If AC voltage is confirmed and the unit still does not cool well on AC, take it to a local Norcold dealer for diagnosis.
